statedReasoning: Government bill (vládní návrh, signed by PM Babiš and Minister of Labour and Social Affairs Aleš Juchelka, 18-21 May 2026). Per the fetched full text and důvodová zpráva, the ENTIRE substantive change is one sentence: Čl. I replaces the amount "350 000 Kč" with "400 000 Kč" in §30 odst. 1 of zákon č. 117/1995 Sb. (state social support act) — the total rodičovský příspěvek (parental allowance) paid to a parent caring for the youngest child in a family, doubled to 800,000 Kč for twins/multiples (unchanged mechanic). Čl. II (transitional) restricts the higher amount to children born or taken into permanent substitute care from 1 January 2027 onward; children born before that date remain permanently at the current 350,000 Kč. Čl. III sets effectiveness at 1 January 2027. The DZ states this follows the Government's Programové prohlášení, which explicitly names raising the parental allowance among its family-support measures. Stated fiscal impact (for the chosen 'new births only' scope): ~0.23 bn Kč in 2027, rising to ~3.57 bn Kč/yr by 2030; the DZ also discloses, as supplementary information, that applying the same +50,000 Kč to ALL current and future recipients (not just post-2027 births) would cost ~7.29 bn Kč in 2027 alone — a broader option the government did not choose, citing budget constraints. No new duties, no change to the benefit's legal structure, eligible-persons circle, or administrative procedure. Section 9 (corruption-risk assessment) states the measure creates no space for corrupt conduct; Section 13 states the predkladatel identified no lobbying activity under the lobbying-regulation law regarding this bill.
researchedContext: Legislative history (psp.cz historie.sqw) confirms an unusually fast track for a parametric benefit bill: submitted by government 22 May 2026, Social Policy Committee (VSP) designated garanční 27 May 2026, first reading 2 June 2026 (21st session), VSP recommended approval 10 June 2026, second reading 30 June 2026, THIRD READING APPROVED 8 July 2026 (vote #285, resolution #249), forwarded to the Senate as Senate print 262 on 9 July 2026, and the Senate's Constitutional-Legal Committee already recommended approval 22 July 2026 — scheduled for the Senate's 28th plenary session beginning 29 July 2026, i.e. potential final enactment within about ten weeks of introduction. Cross-bill comparison (siblingCollisionGroups lists other bills amending 117/1995: 112, 121, 124): tisk 121 — independently re-fetched and read in full for this verdict (idd=268020) — is a KDU-ČSL-led (Jurečka et al.) three-law family package submitted 2 March 2026 that ALSO amends §30 odst. 1 of 117/1995 from '350 000 Kč' to '400 000 Kč' verbatim (Čl. III bod 1), effective from an EARLIER date (1 July 2026 per its Čl. IV), plus two further changes tisk 198 does NOT include: lifting the 70% cap on the monthly draw rate (§30 odst. 3) and loosening the childcare-attendance condition (§31 odst. 3). The Government formally opposed tisk 121 ('nesouhlas', distributed as tisk 121/1, 31 March 2026) and, per its own psp.cz history page, tisk 121 has NOT advanced past committee referral as of 24 July 2026 (only 'further proceedings possible since 10 April 2026' with three pending amendments — no first reading recorded). Seven weeks after rejecting tisk 121, the same Government introduced tisk 198, carrying only the single, cheapest, most electorally salient number from the rejected package (the 350k→400k headline), and fast-tracked it to a Senate floor vote within ten weeks while the broader opposition package it echoes remains stalled pre-first-reading. This is a legislative-process finding, not a self-dealing conflict: an incumbent capturing the popular parametric element of a rival bill it formally opposed, via its own vehicle, while declining the costlier accompanying provisions.

unstatedEffects.effect: The transitional clause (Čl. II) ties the higher 400,000 Kč amount strictly to a child's birth/adoption date (on or after 1 Jan 2027), not to when the family is actually drawing the benefit. A family whose youngest child was born, say, in December 2026 will draw at most 350,000 Kč over the following ~3 years even though they overlap in time with families of children born days later drawing 400,000 Kč for an equivalent care period — a birthdate cliff-edge inequity the DZ frames purely as a budget-scoping choice, without acknowledging the distributional unfairness among contemporaneously-drawing cohorts.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Parents of children born on/after 1 January 2027, relative to parents of children born shortly before that date who receive a lower total benefit for a comparable caregiving period.

unstatedEffects.effect: The Government adopted the identical headline parametric number (350,000→400,000 Kč) that it formally opposed seven weeks earlier in a broader opposition-sponsored package (tisk 121), while omitting that package's more contested and costlier companion provisions (the 70%→100% monthly draw-rate liberalization and the §31 childcare-hours loosening), and moved its narrower version to a Senate vote in roughly ten weeks versus the rival bill's stalled pre-first-reading status as of the same date.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: The submitting Government/Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, which captures political credit for the popular number via its own vehicle rather than the opposition bill that first proposed it; ordinary recipient families receive the same Kč amount regardless of which bill delivers it.

conflictAssessment: No plausible self-dealing channel. This is a universal parametric change to a state social-support benefit paid by ÚP ČR directly to individual parents based on statutory eligibility (caring for a youngest child under 3, or 4 for pre-2024 births) — not a procurement, subsidy, or contract mechanism through which any named company could be paid. Sponsor/co-signer Aleš Juchelka's recorded money ties (ČESKÁ TELEVIZE and ČESKÝ ROZHLAS — both correctly flagged in this batch's municipalExcludedCompanies as public-service broadcasters, not private beneficiaries; YOU STORY UP! s.r.o. and OCCAM PR s.r.o., both PR/communications agencies; a generic zero-value 'OSVČ' self-employment marker) show no connection whatsoever to family social-support administration, benefit disbursement, or the state social-support statute's subject matter. The honest finding, consistent with batch-001's calibration, is the absence of a conflict — the value here is instead the cross-bill legislative-process signal (a government bill echoing and outpacing a rival package it opposed), not a money-ties story.

citations.claim: Tisk 198 (vládní návrh) amends only §30 odst. 1 of zákon č. 117/1995 Sb., replacing '350 000 Kč' with '400 000 Kč' as the total parental allowance for the youngest child (doubled to 800,000 Kč for multiples), effective 1 Jan 2027 and limited by Čl. II to children born/taken into care from that date onward; stated fiscal impact ~0.23 bn Kč (2027) rising to ~3.57 bn Kč/yr (2030) under this scope, versus a disclosed but unchosen ~7.29 bn Kč (2027) if applied to all current recipients. No lobbying identified, no corruption risk found by the predkladatel's own assessment.

Legislative history: government submission 22 May 2026, VSP garanční 27 May, first reading 2 June, VSP approval recommendation 10 June, second reading 30 June, third reading approved 8 July 2026 (vote #285, resolution #249), sent to Senate as print 262 on 9 July, ÚPV Senate committee approved 22 July, scheduled for the Senate's 28th session from 29 July 2026.

Tisk 121 (Jurečka/KDU-ČSL group, submitted 2 March 2026) independently confirmed to amend the same §30 odst. 1 of 117/1995 from '350 000 Kč' to '400 000 Kč' (Čl. III bod 1), effective 1 July 2026 per Čl. IV, plus a §30 odst. 3 draw-rate-cap removal and a §31 odst. 3 childcare-condition rewrite not present in tisk 198.

Tisk 121 legislative history: government issued a formal 'nesouhlas' (disapproval) opinion 31 March 2026 (print 121/1); as of 24 July 2026 the bill remains at the pre-first-reading committee-referral stage (three amendments pending, no reading recorded since organizational-committee referral 2 April 2026).
The amended statute is zákon č. 117/1995 Sb., o státní sociální podpoře — a real, in-force Czech law.
